spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

---

**¶1:** At the time when the primordial Divine Human [GAP-1] descended into the natural degree, he entrusted governing authority to his five [GAP-2] essential spiritual faculties. The divine rational principle and the celestial affection from which spiritual life proceeds [GAP-3] — for the whole governing order of the mind became fixed and held captive within natural states [GAP-4]. Wisdom and falsity were diffused and intermingled with one another — wisdom bound within falsity, and falsity pervading what belongs to wisdom.

**¶2:** At that time the divine rational principle summoned one of its faculties, one abundantly endowed with spiritual power, and entrusted to it the ordering of all external truths. Now this faculty itself [GAP-5] of [GAP-6] established and set those truths in their proper arrangement [GAP-7] proceeding from the divine wisdom of the celestial degree [GAP-8] and set all things into order [GAP-9]. It opened [GAP-10] the ten successive discrete degrees of the spiritual mind [GAP-11], the revolving arrangement of knowledges of good and truth in the external understanding [GAP-12], and these together with the [GAP-13].

**¶3:** The divine rational principle operates in this manner: just as [GAP-14] an architect who builds a dwelling place for the Lord — the regenerated mind — and divides it into distinct faculties and [GAP-15] distinct capacities, furnishing everything required for the harmony of goods and truths [GAP-16], purifying each one; and also the foundational natural truths [GAP-17] are arranged for the beauty and loveliness of spiritual order; he disposes them and perfects them so that when the Lord comes and takes up his indwelling presence within that mind, he might be glorified there.

**¶4:** Furthermore, the divine wisdom of the celestial degree resembles a wise and skilled intelligence [GAP-18] — before the natural mind had been formed [GAP-19], before it had been established and made beautiful and [GAP-20] — this shaping intelligence [GAP-21] works within natural good, but [GAP-22] holds it within his [GAP-23] interior vision, within his understanding. He brings the truths that divide and the truths that cut away what is superfluous, and separates the natural good into distinct kinds [GAP-24], and draws forth [GAP-25] and refines it with the truth that smooths, and makes it even. He fashions many [GAP-26] forms of natural good shaped for use, arranging them kind by kind; he divides and produces from the unformed good vessels and containing forms of every variety — receiving forms, holding forms. This natural good, which [GAP-27] — since previously it had not been shaped before it was sealed by the intelligence and wisdom of this active divine understanding — he distinguished it into different forms of charity and use, each one serviceable to the Lord.

**¶5:** So it is also with the divine wisdom of the celestial degree. In his wisdom he has [GAP-28] arranged the faculties [GAP-29] of the regenerated mind [GAP-30] within it, and within [GAP-31] serviceable forms [GAP-32], the vessels of wisdom that convey divine truth [GAP-33], and all the other forms of use [GAP-34] within the [GAP-35] — so that when the great Lord comes, he who is the divine proceeding in its mediating and redeeming function, who [GAP-36] might take up his indwelling presence in this ordered spiritual realm [GAP-37].

**¶6:** [GAP-38] — the state of spiritual life. The wisdom, however, that is within the formed mind [GAP-39] — the divine intelligence receives it and elevates it to the heavenly kingdom; but what is evil and false, the refuse and the darkness, is gathered together and cast down into hell.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: At the time when the F[ir]st [Man went down] he gave the leadership to his five [sons, and to the] Living Spirit and the Mother of Life [were called forth] as the entire ruling-power is entwined and crucified [in the darkness, and] they were poured out and mixed with each other, the light with the darkness and the darkness with the light.

At that time the Living Spirit called one of his sons, one rich with power. He gave to him the leadership of the garments. Now, he himself [took charge] of [them, and] he hung them and set them up [by the command] of the Father of Life [And then] he set up all things [in order. And] he opened [up the] ten firmaments [and also] the wheel of the stars [and he set] them and the [luminaries].

The Living Spirit is like this: Just as [a builder] and an architect who might build a dwelling for the king, and divide it up into separate houses and [separate chambers] everything that is required for beauty [of the palace] and he cleans them. And also the stones [he prepares] them for beauty and loveliness, and he arranges them and makes them so that should the king come and inhabit that palace, he might glorify him.

Furthermore, the Father of Life resembles a wise and skilled carpenter [who finds a tree] before it was worked [and fashioned] before it was established and made beautiful and [adorned. This] carpenter [does not first] works in it, but [he first sees it] in him in his [mind] in his understanding, and he brings the saw and the adze, and cuts it into separate pieces [and he shapes] it and he pulls the [rough from] it with the plane and he smooths it. He shall make many [sorts of] wooden implements, arranging them shape by shape; he cuts and produces wooden implements from it, wooden implements of different kinds, (such as) dishes, bowls. This wood, that [is now formed] since previously it had not been worked before it was sealed by [the ski]ll and wisdom of this dextrous carpenter. He cut it up into different sorts of implements useful to his master.

So is it also with the Father of Life. In his wisdom he has [fashioned all things] in limbs [and built this] palace [and set all things] in it or in a [form] useful [and he made] the ships of light [and also] all the other works [that are] in the [heavens] so that when the great king comes, he who is the Third Ambassador, who [shall come, that] he might dwell in this universe [and be glorified]
[that all things may] live. The light, however, that is in it [is purified by the] wise, and he takes it up to the land; but the waste and the darkness will be gathered and thrown down to the abyss.

fills.explanation: The spiritual reading says "descended into the natural degree," which in Manichaean cosmological vocabulary is the First Man going down to battle the darkness.
The sentence requires a connective listing the recipients of leadership: five sons, and also the Living Spirit and Mother of Life.

In Manichaean cosmology the Living Spirit and Mother of Life were evoked/called forth by the Father of Greatness; the spiritual reading marks this as the point where these faculties proceed into action.
The spiritual reading says "held captive within natural states" — in Manichaean register, the ruling-power was crucified in the darkness, and then the elements were poured out and mixed.
The son was given leadership of the garments, so "he himself took charge" describes his assuming authority, matching the spiritual reading's sense of the faculty ordering external truths.
The pronoun "them" refers back to the garments already mentioned, and the connective "and" transitions to the next action of hanging and setting up.
The spiritual reading says "proceeding from the divine wisdom of the celestial degree," which in the Kephalaia's natural register is expressed as acting by the command of the Father of Life.
A simple temporal connective bridging the Father of Life's authority to the next action of setting up all things, matching the spiritual reading's sequential ordering.
The spiritual reading says "set all things into order," and the text then transitions to opening the firmaments — "in order" completes the action and "And" provides the connective.
The verb "opened" requires an article before "ten firmaments," and "opened up" is the natural expression for spreading out the heavens in cosmological construction language.

A connective linking the ten firmaments to the next cosmic element (the wheel of stars), matching the spiritual reading's enumeration of successive degrees and then the revolving arrangement of knowledges.

The Living Spirit set the cosmic elements in place; "he set them" connects the wheel of stars to its arrangement among the firmaments, matching the spiritual reading's sense of these being placed together.
After firmaments and the wheel of stars, the remaining major cosmic feature in Manichaean cosmology is the luminaries (sun and moon), corresponding to the spiritual reading's final cosmic element.

The text says "Just as [GAP-14] and an architect," requiring a paired craftsman noun; "a builder and an architect" is a natural Kephalaia-style pairing for one who constructs the dwelling for the king.
Parallel to "separate houses," the architectural term "separate chambers" corresponds to the spiritual reading's "distinct capacities" within the dwelling/mind.

The architect is building a dwelling/palace for the king, so "beauty of the palace" specifies what the beauty pertains to, matching the spiritual reading's harmony of goods and truths within the mind.
The stones (foundational natural truths) require preparation before being set for beauty; "he prepares them" fits the architectural sequence and the spiritual reading's "are arranged for the beauty."

The carpenter parable requires introducing the raw material; the spiritual reading describes unformed natural good, which in the Kephalaia's natural register is an unworked tree that the carpenter discovers and will fashion.
The passage lists the tree's unworked states in parallel "before" clauses; "worked and fashioned" pairs naturally, matching the spiritual reading's "formed" before being "established."

Completing the list of unachieved states (beautiful and adorned), then transitioning with "This" back to the carpenter subject who begins his work, matching the spiritual reading's shift to "this shaping intelligence."

The "but" that follows creates a contrast: the carpenter does not first work physically but first conceives the design in his mind, matching the spiritual reading's emphasis on interior vision preceding outward formation.

The carpenter first conceives the design mentally; "he first sees it in him in his mind" matches the spiritual reading's "holds it within his interior vision" — the interior perception before outward work.

The parallel construction "in his mind, in his understanding" creates a doublet of interior perception, matching the spiritual reading's "interior vision" — the mind is the seat of the carpenter's design.
In the carpentry sequence — cutting into pieces, then shaping — "and he shapes it" is the next step before planing, matching the spiritual reading's progression of separating into distinct kinds.
A carpenter pulls the roughness from the wood using a plane; "draws forth" in the spiritual reading corresponds to removing what is superfluous, and the plane removes the rough surface.
The carpenter makes many varieties of wooden implements; "many sorts of" matches the spiritual reading's "forms of natural good shaped for use" and parallels the later phrase "different kinds."

The wood is described in its transformed state after the carpenter's work; "is now formed" contrasts with "previously it had not been worked," matching the spiritual reading's description of natural good now shaped.

The Father of Life, like the carpenter, has fashioned all things in the cosmic body; the spiritual reading says "arranged the faculties," and "fashioned" continues the carpenter metaphor applied cosmically.
Connecting "limbs" (faculties) to the "palace" (regenerated mind/cosmos), "and built this palace" continues the architectural metaphor from ¶3 applied to the Father of Life's cosmic work.
After building the palace, the Father of Life set all things within it, matching the spiritual reading's sense of ordering the contents of the regenerated mind.
The text describes things arranged "in a form useful," matching the spiritual reading's "serviceable forms" — each element placed in a distinct form of use.
A connective introducing the next cosmic feature; "and he made the ships of light" describes the Father of Life fashioning the vessels of wisdom (sun and moon) that convey divine truth.
A connective listing additional cosmic works alongside the ships of light, matching the spiritual reading's enumeration of "the vessels of wisdom... and all the other forms of use."
A relative clause connecting "all the other works" to their location; "that are in the heavens" describes where these cosmic forms of use are arranged.
The location of all the cosmic works — firmaments, stars, ships of light — is the heavens, corresponding to the spiritual reading's ordered spiritual realm where all forms of use are placed.
The Third Ambassador's coming initiates the purpose of the cosmic construction; "who shall come, that he might dwell" expresses the divine proceeding's arrival to take up indwelling presence.
Paralleling ¶3 where the king enters the palace and "might glorify him," the Third Ambassador's indwelling results in glorification — the culmination of the cosmic ordering.
The purpose clause concluding the cosmic narrative: the Ambassador dwells and is glorified so that all things may live, matching the spiritual reading's "the state of spiritual life."

The light within the cosmos is purified by the wise one (divine intelligence) who then elevates it to the heavenly land, matching the spiritual reading's "the divine intelligence receives it and elevates it."
